mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines in the next 20 days but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% indicates labor market deterioration that precedes economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) and housing starts (HOUST < 1000) signal a broad economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Both INDPRO < 105 and HOUST < 1000 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: In the housing bust phase (HOUST < 1000), retail sales above 370,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 370000) indicate resilient consumer demand that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the housing bust phase (HOUST < 1000), RSAFS > 370000 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A declining non-farm payrolls level (PAYEMS) signals labor market weakness that precedes equity market downturns, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS declines in the next 5 days but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1000 thousand units (HOUST < 1000) indicate a contracting housing market that signals economic weakness and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1000 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate cuts (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) signal an active monetary policy response to economic distress, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 3.0 and UNRATE > 4.5 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP level below 12,000 billion dollars (GDPC1 < 12000) indicates a recessionary economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 < 12000 but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases.
